territorial_scope.description: Applies to Utah state courts, magistrates, prosecuting attorneys and the Board of Pardons and Parole under Utah criminal justice statutes.

evidence.quote: including the Utah Office for Victims of Crime

summary.short: Amends Utah criminal justice provisions so that courts, magistrates and the Board of Pardons and Parole may not rely solely on an algorithm or risk assessment tool score in diversion, sentencing, pretrial release, probation and parole decisions. Effective May 1, 2024.
summary.long: House Bill 366 (2024) amends several Utah criminal justice statutes in Sections 9 to 14 of the bill and takes effect May 1, 2024 (Section 15). In each amended section, the court, magistrate or board may not rely solely on an algorithm or risk assessment tool score: in approving a diversion agreement (77-2-5(11)), in determining the appropriate sentence (77-18-103(9)), in determining pretrial release (77-20-205(9)(b)), in deciding whether parole should be granted or terminated (77-27-5(8)), and in probation decisions (77-18-105(9)(b)). Other amendments require a presentence investigation report to include findings from any screening and assessment of the defendant (77-18-103(2)(c)), cap a diversion program at two years (77-2-5(10)), and require the court to consider a defendant's ability to pay a diversion fee on request, with the fee not to exceed the suggested fine in the Uniform Fine Schedule (77-2-5(7), (9)). Section 14 requires the Administrative Office of the Courts to submit case data to the Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice every six months, including a convicted defendant's total pretrial risk assessment score (78A-2-109.5(2)(i), (3)). The bill text provided contains no separate penalty or enforcement provisions.
